WHELCHEL, 673-6196. MATTER ARGUED. RULING AFTER HEARING: PLAINTIFF FLORSHEIM BROTHERS' MOTION TO COMPEL DEFENDANT PG&E'S DEPOSITIONS AND PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS BY DEPONENT IS DENIED. AS TO THE DISCOVERY SOUGHT PURSUANT TO THE ALLEGATIONS RELATING TO CPUC SECTION 2106, THE MOTION IS DENIED. CPUC SECTION 2106 ESTABLISHES A BASIS FOR RECOVERING PUNITIVE DAMAGES NOT ARISING OUT OF A CONTRACT. IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH A DIFFERENT PROCEDURE FOR OBTAINING DISCOVERY. THEREFORE, IT IS NECESSARY TO PROCEED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF CC SECTION 3295. PLAINTIFF HAS NOT MADE APPLICATION TO THE COURT TO PROCEED BASED UPON THE PROVISIONS OF THAT SECTION, AND THE MOTION TO COMPEL IS DENIED. THE ABSENCE OF A SEPARATE STATEMENT MAKES IT IMPOSSIBLE TO DETERMINE EACH OF THE SPECIFIC CLAIMS OF DEFENDANT'S FAILURE TO PROVIDE PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE TESTIMONY. BASED UPON THE LATENESS OF THE MOTION, THE PENDENCY OF TRIAL IN LESS THAN TWO WEEKS, THE LACK OF DILIGENCE IN PURSUING THIS TESTIMONY IN THE FACE OF PREVIOUS OBJECTIONS, AND THE LACK OF SUFFICIENT SPECIFICITY, THE MOTION IS DENIED AS IT SEEKS FURTHER PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE. THIS ORDER IS MADE WITHOUT DETERMINING THE ADEQUACY OF THE WITNESSES AND TESTIMONY OFFERED BY PG&E IN RESPONSE TO 24 TOPICS WHERE ADDITIONAL PERSONS MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE WERE PRODUCED IN RESPONSE TO THE SUBJECT NOTICES OF DEPOSITION. COMM: EVERETT A. HEWLETT
